properties.statement: A STALE `.reflow2/kit-version.json` IS NOT A WRONG VERSION LABEL — IT IS AN INPUT TO A LIVE DECISION, AND THAT COST WAS THE ⚠️ LEFT UNVERIFIED IN `fact:updating-reflow2-does-not-update-a-project-already-set-up`. That node closed with two open ⚠️ items, one of them: 'Whether a stale kit costs anything concrete — NOT VERIFIED.' This answers it with a first concrete cost, read out of the source rather than inferred. `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs:175` — `recorded_harnesses()` — READS `.reflow2/kit-version.json` and pulls `harnesses` out of it, and `nudge.rs:151` branches on the answer: a project whose recorded harnesses do not include `claude` is told `NoHookForThisHarness` (its harness cannot have a nudge), and only `None`/matching falls through to `Absent` (a real gap worth reporting). SO THE RECEIPT OF AN INSTALL EVENT IS BEING READ AS A LIVE FACT ABOUT THE PROJECT, which is precisely the misreading the parent fact identifies one layer up ('a receipt for an install EVENT, not a live reading') — recorded there about humans reading it, true here of reflow2's own code reading it. OBSERVED, 2026-08-14, Alex's home machine via his Grok 4.6 session (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md): live MCP 0.31.0, sidecar 0.11.0 / 0ec473e dated 2026-07-25 — twenty versions of drift — and the same session's self-assessment records 'I did not install the loop nudge; loop_status was called by hand', which is the downstream symptom sitting one line from its own cause without the two being connected. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the file is read; the read decides which of three nudge answers a project gets; that project's copy is twenty versions old. WHAT IS NOT: whether his stamp actually lacks a `harnesses` key (a 0.11.0 stamp predates `--harness`, so it most likely returns `None` and falls through to the SAFE branch) — i.e. THE BUG MAY NOT HAVE BITTEN HIM YET. That is the honest reading and it does not make the coupling safe: the branch that misfires is the one where an OLD stamp names harnesses that a NEWER kit would name differently, and nothing anywhere compares the stamp's generation against the binary answering the call. THE ASYMMETRY THAT HIDES IT is already on the record in the parent fact: `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit` is a SYMLINK to the checkout on the maintainer's box and a frozen tarball for a consumer, so the maintainer's stamp cannot go stale by construction. FIX SHAPES, smallest first: have the nudge treat a stamp older than the running binary as `None` (unknown) rather than as an answer, since this module's own doc comment at nudge.rs:170 already argues that not-knowing and knowing-it-is-absent must not share a reply; or surface the kit generation next to the binary version so a human sees the split; or restamp on `reflow2 update`.
